statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: An individual whose Georgia conviction has been pardoned by the State Board of Pardons and Paroles may petition the court in which the conviction occurred to restrict access to the criminal history record information. The offense must not have been a serious violent felony as defined in § 17-10-6.1 or a sexual offense as defined in § 17-10-6.2, the individual must not have been convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction, excluding nonserious traffic offenses, since the pardon was granted, and must have no pending charged offenses. The court shall grant the order if the harm otherwise resulting to the individual clearly outweighs the public's interest in the information being publicly available. The pardon is the starting event and there is no waiting period independent of it. Restriction limits who may see criminal history record information; it does not destroy the record and gives no right to deny that a restricted conviction exists.
doNotImport: Do not quote a filing fee or a pauper's-affidavit rule; whether a Georgia clerk charges a fee for a filing in an existing criminal case, and whether O.C.G.A. § 9-15-2 reaches it, are recorded as unresolved and county-specific.
Do not begin this route before a pardon exists; the pardon application itself is outside scope.
Do not decide whether the offense is a serious violent felony under § 17-10-6.1 or a sexual offense under § 17-10-6.2; the exclusions are applied to a Code section and a dispute is a stop.
Do not promise that restriction destroys the record, prevents disqualification in the manner of a first-offender discharge under § 42-8-63.1, or supersedes disclosure required by federal law.
Do not write the participant's own statement of what has changed; the packet formats what the participant supplies and assesses none of it.
Do not hardcode a court, county, case number, OTN, judge, pardon date or prosecuting attorney; every one is a case fact from the participant's own record.
Do not extend this family to the misdemeanor-conviction route or to the sealing-only route; each has its own track.

the statement that there has been no conviction of any crime in any jurisdiction, excluding nonserious traffic offenses, since the pardon was granted

name and mailing address of the District Attorney or Solicitor-General for the county, and the clerk of court, served and certified

finalVerificationRequirements: Confirm that a pardon exists and copy its date from the pardon certificate issued by the State Board of Pardons and Paroles; this route begins once a pardon exists.

Copy the convicting court and its level, county, case number, OTN, arrest date and exact O.C.G.A. Code section from the final disposition, the case papers and the Georgia criminal history report, never from memory.
Read every numbered statement in the petition; each is pleaded as the petitioner's own statement, and any that is not true is a reason not to file.
Confirm the filing method, any fee, any pauper's-affidavit practice and any standing preference on proposed orders with the clerk of the convicting court before filing; the packet quotes no figure.
Confirm the prosecuting attorney and clerk of court to be served, serve by certified mail, e-filing or hand delivery, and complete the certificate only when the copies actually go out.
The petitioner signs and dates the petition and certificate as Defendant, Pro Se where unrepresented; the judge's name, SO ORDERED date and signature block are never pre-filled.

filingDestination.statement: File in the existing criminal case with the clerk of the convicting court, under the existing case number, styled State of Georgia v. Defendant. Confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing: no statewide judiciary form exists, local courts control their own filing and e-filing practice, some clerks resist accepting motions in closed criminal cases, and some judges have standing preferences on proposed orders.

feeAndWaiver.statement: No statutory filing fee is identified. Because the relief is a petition in an existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, the leading Georgia pro se practice does not budget one; whether any Georgia clerk charges a fee for such a filing is unresolved and county-specific, so no figure is quoted and the participant asks the clerk of the convicting court before filing.
feeAndWaiver.waiverStatement: Unresolved: the pauper's affidavit route under O.C.G.A. § 9-15-2 is designed for civil actions and its application to a filing in a criminal case is not established; the participant asks the same clerk.
feeAndWaiver.sourceOfRule: GA.memo.json track ga-pardon-j7, rules.fees, rules.feeWaiver and the unresolved fee question

serviceAndNotice.statement: Notice to the prosecuting attorney, identified as District Attorney or Solicitor-General for the county; practice also serves the clerk of court. Serve by certified mail, e-filing or hand delivery, certified in the certificate of service. A hearing, where requested, is held within 90 days.

postFilingTimeline.step: File the petition, proposed order, certificate and exhibits with the clerk of the convicting court in the existing criminal case, and serve the prosecuting attorney and the clerk of court.
postFilingTimeline.timing: once the pardon exists; there is no waiting period independent of it, and there must have been no conviction of any crime in any jurisdiction, excluding nonserious traffic offenses, since it was granted

postFilingTimeline.step: Where a hearing is requested, the court holds it within 90 days of filing; the prosecuting attorney may oppose.
postFilingTimeline.timing: within 90 days of filing where a hearing is requested

postFilingTimeline.step: The court decides whether the harm otherwise resulting to the individual clearly outweighs the public's interest and, if so, enters the order directing GCIC and the county agencies to restrict.
postFilingTimeline.timing: after any hearing; the finding is the court's

participantChecklist.text: Obtain the pardon certificate from the State Board of Pardons and Paroles and copy its date; do not file while still seeking the pardon.
Gather the final disposition and, where relied on, the Georgia criminal history report, and fill every dotted blank from them.
Read every numbered statement in the petition; each is pleaded as your own, and if any is not true of your case do not file.
Confirm the filing method, any fee, any pauper's-affidavit practice and any proposed-order preference with the clerk of the convicting court before filing.
Sign and date the petition yourself as Defendant, Pro Se where unrepresented; serve the prosecuting attorney and the clerk of court, and complete the certificate only when the copies actually go out.
